title: Debias-SparseGPT: Pruning a Model Can Amplify Its Biases
hook: Compression isn't neutral. Weight sparsification has been shown to amplify existing bias, with outputs swinging on persona cues — so this method adds a debiasing term to the pruning objective itself.
key_points: Prior work found SparseGPT-style sparsification can amplify existing model bias, with outputs varying by persona cues in the prompt.
Debias-SparseGPT is post-training pruning with a second-order term defined over demographically contrasting inputs.
The debiasing is representational — it acts on how the pruned weights reshape representations, not on outputs after the fact.
Across models and 25%, 50%, and structured 2:4 sparsity it reduces pruning-induced bias versus SparseGPT while preserving perplexity and zero-shot accuracy.
Under the harshest 2:4 pattern, adding long-context, content-rich examples to the calibration set improved both performance and fairness.
content_html: Pruning and quantization are usually discussed as accuracy-versus-cost trades: how much perplexity do you give up for how much speed. Proskurina and colleagues start from a less comfortable finding in recent work — that weight sparsification methods such as SparseGPT can amplify a model's existing biases, with outputs shifting noticeably depending on persona cues in the prompt — and argue the pruning objective should account for it.
extra_html:
How it works

Debias-SparseGPT is a post-training pruning method that adds representational debiasing via a second-order term defined over demographically contrasting inputs. Because it stays within the post-training pruning framework, it keeps the computational profile that makes such methods attractive in the first place — no full retraining.

Why it matters

The authors validate across a range of generative LLMs and sparsity regimes — 25%, 50%, and structured 2:4 — and report consistently reduced pruning-induced bias relative to SparseGPT while preserving perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Under 2:4 structured sparsity, the pattern that degrades quality most aggressively, augmenting the calibration set with long-context, content-rich examples improved both downstream performance and fairness. The broader takeaway for anyone shipping compressed models: standard benchmarks can stay flat while behavior you weren't measuring moves.
